question: Where does fertilization of the egg normally happen in the body?
explanation: The ampulla is the widest part of the fallopian tube where the sperm and egg usually meet. [learn more](BMP210_U4_T2#BMP210_U4_T2_h1)

question: Why do so many sperm fail to reach the egg on their journey through the female reproductive tract?

options.A: Rapid absorption into the uterine wall lining
options.B: Hostile acidic vaginal environment and physical barriers
options.C: Immediate destruction by the ovary before entering the tube
options.D: Lack of seminal fluid to propel them past the cervix

explanation: The vagina is naturally acidic, and thick mucus at the cervix traps or stops most sperm before they make it to the tubes. [learn more](BMP210_U4_T2#BMP210_U4_T2_h1)

question: What is the main purpose of sperm capacitation inside the female reproductive tract?

options.A: To enable the sperm to fertilize the oocyte
options.B: To protect the sperm from immediate vaginal acidity
options.C: To guide the sperm directly into the ovary
options.D: To help the sperm multiply in number before reaching the egg

explanation: Capacitation changes the sperm membrane and movement so it gains the strength and ability to fertilize an egg. [learn more](BMP210_U4_T2#BMP210_U4_T2_h2)

question: A patient asks how long sperm can survive and wait for ovulation in the female tract. What is the best response?
explanation: Capacitated sperm can live in the female tract for up to five days, which is why intercourse a few days before ovulation can still result in pregnancy. [learn more](BMP210_U4_T2#BMP210_U4_T2_h2)

question: Which enzyme is released by the sperm to help it digest a path through the outer layer of the egg?
explanation: Acrosin is a specialized enzyme stored in the sperm head that breaks down the protective outer layer of the egg. [learn more](BMP210_U4_T2#BMP210_U4_T2_h3)

question: What triggers a sperm cell to start releasing its digestive enzymes?

options.A: Physical friction against the walls of the fallopian tube
options.B: Exposure to the alkaline fluid inside the uterine cavity
options.C: Chemical signals released directly from the mature ovary
options.D: Contact with the specific proteins of the zona pellucida

explanation: Touching the outer layer of the egg causes the sperm to release its enzymes so it can break through. [learn more](BMP210_U4_T2#BMP210_U4_T2_h3)

question: What exact event happens right after the sperm successfully breaks through the outer shell of the egg?

options.A: Disintegration of the remaining corona radiata
options.B: Cleavage of the zygote into four distinct cells
options.C: Fusion of the sperm and oocyte plasma membranes
options.D: Immediate breakdown of the entire uterine lining

explanation: Once through the outer layer, the outer membrane of the sperm touches and fuses with the membrane of the egg. [learn more](BMP210_U4_T2#BMP210_U4_T2_h4)

question: Which cellular event is triggered inside the egg the moment a sperm enters its cytoplasm?

options.A: Reversal of the first mitotic cell division
options.B: Immediate replication of maternal DNA strands
options.C: Destruction of the cell nucleus to form a blastocyst
options.D: Completion of the second meiotic division

explanation: Sperm entry acts as a signal for the egg to finish its final cell division process. [learn more](BMP210_U4_T2#BMP210_U4_T2_h4)

question: What is the main danger if more than one sperm fertilizes an egg?

options.A: Premature shedding of the uterine decidua
options.B: An abnormal and fatal number of chromosomes
options.C: Immediate implantation outside the uterine cavity
options.D: Complete failure of the placenta to develop

explanation: If multiple sperm enter the egg, it introduces too many chromosomes, which prevents normal human development. [learn more](BMP210_U4_T2#BMP210_U4_T2_h5)

question: Which cellular change helps prevent more than one sperm from entering the egg?

options.A: Complete cessation of maternal heartbeat and circulation
options.B: Rapid dissolution of the entire secondary oocyte membrane
options.C: Hardening and modification of the zona pellucida by cortical granule enzymes
options.D: Instantaneous shedding of all remaining follicular cells

explanation: Enzymes from the egg quickly change the outer shell so extra sperm can no longer attach or enter. [learn more](BMP210_U4_T2#BMP210_U4_T2_h5)

question: What is formed the exact moment the male and female genetic material combine?
explanation: The single cell formed when the male and female genetic materials join together is called a zygote. [learn more](BMP210_U4_T2#BMP210_U4_T2_h6)

question: Why is restoring the normal chromosome count during fertilization important for the baby?

options.A: It ensures the baby receives the correct total of forty-six chromosomes
options.B: It stops the mother from experiencing early pregnancy symptoms
options.C: It prevents the placenta from attaching too deeply into the uterus
options.D: It guarantees that the baby will develop into a male child

explanation: Combining 23 chromosomes from the sperm and 23 from the egg gives the baby the normal total of 46 needed for healthy growth. [learn more](BMP210_U4_T2#BMP210_U4_T2_h6)
